Optional data-kind silhouette/ridge/valley (ridge and valley only label the sign), data-mirror="x", data-op="smooth", data-profile="bowl" on a polygon; stroke-width is only drawn. Resolved as a file, then under ixdar-app and src/main/resources/, then on the classpath (e.g. dsl/skull/pass1.svg). outputs.description: One line for the pass (vertices in and after refinement), then one per stroke: its kind, cell, radius, depth, points lifted and dropped (grazing, off-surface, out of cell), vertices moved and peak displacement; a stroke that moved nothing is marked DROPPED with the reason.

nodes.description: A sculpt's one stroke pass on its base: every stroke is a curve held on the base mesh by the sidecar beside the SVG (ixdar-cli sculpt-sync writes both; without one the SVG's strokes are lifted onto the base through the camera the SVG stores), the faces they reach are refined once, then every stroke's move is summed on the base, distinct strokes adding. It refuses an input that is already a stroke_sculpt output: a second pass is a new DSL on the sculpt saved as a new base. The stroke alone sets what moves, in world units: a ridge, valley or fill moves each vertex it sees along the stroke's mean normal by data-depth x w x (1 - (d / data-radius)^2)^2, d the vertex's distance across that normal to the stroke (a fill: the union of its samples' bumps), w 1 except inside a data-profile="bowl" fill, where it is t(2 - t) of the sample's depth in from the outline over the deepest's; the move fades from full where the surface faces the stroke's camera within 60 degrees to none where it turns past 75 degrees, edge-on. A silhouette drags the outline it reaches, within data-radius, all the way onto the stroke; data-op="smooth" smooths within data-radius. Mirror copies of a stroke never add to it; the report output lists every stroke's effect. A chain's points may lie far apart: its falloff and refinement follow the segments between them. Refinement stops at edges of 0.005 (or the base's mean edge / 16), and a falloff of slope 1.54 x |data-depth| / data-radius stairs on edges more than twice data-radius / (3 x that slope), so keep |data-depth| <= data-radius^2 / (2.31 x 0.005): about 0.14 at radius 0.04, 0.55 at 0.08; a fill's samples union into a rim up to twice as steep (about 2.1 x |data-depth| / data-radius at the default spacing) and a bowl's floor rises at 2 x |data-depth| / its deepest inset, so their limits are lower; a steeper stroke terraces and the report marks it TOO STEEP, with the limit. A stroke whose moves would turn faces inside out is marked FOLDS with how many the pass held back and how many stay.
